title: Round 3 — what the fixes introduced or leave open
subtitle: B1 is a merge blocker (CI red, reproduced and A/B-tested locally). N1-N3 are behaviour notes for the maintainers.
lines: ## B1  CI red: Hosted process fault gates / MySQL 8.4 -> HostedProcessCrashIT (FG6C), caused by one line
-- RuntimeBrokerHttpServer.observe(): dropped `&& runtimeProtocol == 3`, so UNKNOWN v2 (file) executions are reconciled too
-- worker-kill: status 409 runtime_execution_evidence_unavailable, gate expects runtime_broker_execution_unknown
-- worker-stop: status 503 managed_runtime_unavailable (retryable), gate expects 200
++ same tree with only that line restored: worker-kill 1/1, worker-stop 1/1; harness-* and spring-kill pass either way
## N1  a reply that can never arrive still ends in a stuck Session, now after 10.5 minutes
-- SSE server restarted 2 s into a 20 s call: execution UNKNOWN at 6.8 s, turn active until 633 s, then blocked
-- tool that never answers on a timeoutMs 5000 server: UNKNOWN at 7.8 s, turn active until 634 s, then blocked
-- both: no terminal event, next prompt 409, detach 503, lease held (F1: Workspace locked), qwen_tool_execution UNKNOWN
== the configured timeoutMs does not shorten the Hosted wait; a lost connection is known at once but still waits 630 s
## N2  one pinned server down -> every turn in the Session fails (refresh before each model request)
-- SSE down: text-only prompt turn_error, stdio-only tool turn turn_error, 0 effects; same with Streamable HTTP down
-- each failed turn adds a failed mcp_configuration revision; the Session recovers once the server returns
## N3  cancellation is deferred: the tool runs to completion and its effect happens
!! prompt cancel at 2.5 s -> turn ends 9.1 s later; with a 10 min tool the user waits up to 10 min (documented by the author)

notes.text: B1 must be resolved before merge: either keep observe() protocol-3-only and reconcile MCP separately, or update the FG6C expectations with a justification. N1/N2 widen the H1 limits the author documented and are worth recording next to them.

title: Round 3 — migrations, mutation, cost and CI
subtitle: Flyway experiment on MySQL 8.4.11 with this PR (V21) and a trial merge with #12894 @ 033c74d3 (V19, V20).
lines: ## Flyway order (V19 -> V21 rename)
++ merged jar on a fresh database: applies 19, 20, 21 and starts
-- this PR first (DB at 21), then the merged jar on the same DB: Detected resolved migration not applied to database: 19
== so #12894 must land first, or whoever lands second renumbers above the other (outOfOrder is not enabled)
## Mutation (6 cli test files, 122 tests)
++ M7 and M11 (round-1 survivors) now killed; X1 cancel, X2 idle sibling close, X4 DELETE bound, X6 wait-through-unknown,
++ X8 intent cancel on close, X10 unchanged-catalog skip, X11 grant renewal: all killed
!! X3   busy retired connection not closed after its last settle (F6)   SURVIVES
!! X5   default request timeout back to 25 s (F4)                       SURVIVES
!! X7   no refresh before each model request (the F2 fix itself)        SURVIVES
!! X9   identity conflicts back to 503                                  SURVIVES
## Cost of refreshing before each model request (text-only turns, load ~25-30)
== 1 server: 1 mcp-discover per prompt, 103-185 ms to first model request; 6 servers: 6 per prompt, 154-232 ms
-- 21 pass, 1 fail (Hosted process fault gates / MySQL 8.4 = B1); Test, Lint, MariaDB, Java matrix green

notes.text: The rename removes the duplicate-version crash; the remaining ordering rule is worth stating in the PR. X7 is the main gap: the refresh-before-inference wiring that fixes F2 is only proven end to end, not by a unit test.
